title: Op-path scout: runtime probe + confidence calibrator for prefill/decode kernel picks
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Kernel selection for inference currently uses a static heuristic based on architecture and historical seqlen buckets. For mixed conversational loads we see higher 99th-percentile latency during bursts and on new request shapes. This ticket adds a lightweight runtime probing layer (scout) that issues microbench probes and maintains a per-op-path confidence score to pick safe, cost-effective kernels for prefill and decode phases separately.
background: Existing systems warmstart from offline profiles and seqlen histograms. But when traffic drifts (new seqlen distributions, different batch shapes, or new hardware variants), static heuristics cause either extra cost (overly conservative picks) or latency regressions (unsafe but cheap kernels). Previous tickets implemented profiling, bayesian picks, and phase-aware selectors, but none include a realtime per-request probe + confidence calibration that explicitly splits prefill and decode decisions with a safety envelope for tail latency.
goals: 1) Reduce 99th-percentile latency for mixed conversational workloads by at least 15% compared to current baseline under drift scenarios. 2) Keep average token cost within 5% of baseline. 3) Provide an explainable confidence score for each kernel pick and a safety fallback when confidence is low. 4) Be production-safe: probe budget <= 2% of requests and probes are non-blocking for SLOs.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end experiment shows >=15% reduction in P99 latency for at least two drift scenarios (long-prefill heavy, burst decode-heavy) on staging.
- Cost-per-token delta <= +5% vs baseline over 24h.
- Probes consume <= 2% of request budget under default config and can be throttled per-customer.
- Rollout plan with canary on 5% traffic and automatic rollback if P50 or P95 regresses >5%.
- Console UI shows per-route confidence heatmap and probe rate metrics.
design_summary: We will add an Op-path Scout service component that: (a) maintains a tiny in-memory table keyed by (model, arch, exec-mode, seqlen-bin, phase) mapping to {preferred-kernel, confidence, last-update}, (b) issues async microbench probes when confidence < threshold or when the sample is new, (c) computes a confidence score combining recency, probe variance, and observed tail latency, (d) exposes a safety envelope configured by SLO budgets (max allowed extra latency), and (e) integrates with prefill/decode scheduler to allow different picks per phase. Probes are executed on a low-priority probe pool to avoid impacting critical capacity. Warmstart uses offline seqlen-arch histograms and previous experiment snapshots.
implementation_plan:
1) Schema & storage: add lightweight Scout store (in-memory + persisted checkpoint to object-store) and migration code.
2) Probe runner: implement microbench harness that can run short synthetic prefill/decode workloads on the candidate kernels, capture mean+tail, and return metrics.
3) Confidence calculator: algorithm combining exponential decay of older probes, Bayesian update on probe results, and variance penalty.
4) Integration with scheduler: API to request preferred-kernel for (model, phase, seqlen), with fallback chain.
5) Safety envelope: implement latency budget check and automatic fallback to safe kernel if predicted tail >= threshold.
6) Telemetry & dashboard: probe rate, probe latency, confidence distribution, pick changes, rollback events.
7) Tests & benchmarks: unit tests, microbench harness tests, staging experiments.
8) Rollout: feature flag gate and progressive canary.

Implementation milestones:
- Week 1: Scout store + API and unit tests.
- Week 2: Probe runner + basic confidence updates.
- Week 3: Integrate with prefill/decode scheduler and run internal bench.
- Week 4: Staging experiments, dashboard, and canary rollout.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for store, API, and confidence math.
- Microbench validation: regression-free on known benchmarks.
- Staging A/B: route 50% baseline vs 50% scout-on, run controlled drift experiments (long-prefill and burst decode), collect P50/P95/P99 and cost.
- Fault injection: deliberately drop probe responses and ensure fallbacks engage.
- Load test: ensure probe runner does not exceed probe-pool capacity and does not affect regular workloads.
rollout:
Feature-flagged rollout:
- Canary 1 (internal): 1% traffic — smoke checks and dashboards.
- Canary 2 (customers): 5% traffic for 48 hours with auto-threshold rollback.
- Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks if metrics stable.
- Emergency rollback plan: disable scout at router level and revert pick API to historical heuristic.
telemetry: Metrics to emit: scout.probes.total, scout.probes.success, scout.probes.latency_ms.p50/p95/p99, scout.confidence.mean, scout.confidence.p10/p90, kernel.pick_changes.count, kernel.fallbacks.count, route.p99_latency.delta, probe.cpu_seconds, probe.node_impact_indicator. Dashboards: per-model and per-region confidence heatmaps and a probe-rate control panel. Alerts: if probe latency or failure >10% or if route.p95 regresses >7% after enabling scout.
risks_mitigations:
- Risk: Probes cause resource contention. Mitigation: run probes on separate low-priority pool with strict concurrency limits and capacity throttle.
- Risk: Confidence model mis-calibrates and picks an unsafe kernel. Mitigation: conservative default safety envelope and immediate fallback to 'safe' kernel; canary rollout.
- Risk: Probe budget increases costs. Mitigation: probe rate cap per-customer and dynamic backoff.
- Risk: Complexity increases debugging surface. Mitigation: structured logs, pick trace IDs attached to responses for postmortem analysis, and UI to replay decisions.
